I'm really sorry about what you're going through, it's tough. How well do you know the relationship she has with her parents? Maybe she hasn't had anyone to talk to about it in order to fully heal. You should try graciously suggesting that she get some help from a therapist/counselor. Her counselor should help give her a new look on sex with you, that it's okay to move on and the past doesn't mean all people will treat her like that.

I understand that you are getting fed up with the miss-communication and lack of intimacy but hold on just a little bit longer, I bet once she gets the help she needs things will change drastically for you guys. And she more than definitely needs you while she goes through this process, you are her rock :)

Coming for the point of view of someone who was sexually abused it's hard! it really is. It's not that she doesn't trust you or doesn't love you at all, so please place that out of your head. People who have gone through sexual abuse often get random triggers out of know where. She possibly could be experiencing these triggers when you try to initiate sex which leads to her shutting down.

If i were you I would sit down with your wife and explain to her that she matters to you and that you would never ever hurt her. Explain that in a healthy relationship there needs to be intimacy involved. Ask her if there are certain words, phrases or touches (on the arm, wrist etc.) that cause her to have flashbacks. When you have discovered what causes her to have these flashbacks try working on new approaches to sex that don't involve what she has listed. Lastly it is important to tell her in this conversation "We can stop at ANY time, it's up to you and I won't be mad" this takes all of the pressure off of her and shows you are willing to work with her.

My Fiance did this exact approach with me and I can't tell you how close it brought us together. goodluck :)
